specification.family_title: Connection recovery and unsafe pool reuse
specification.title: The top-level ROLLBACK of a failed transaction fails on the client; then the next unit of work runs on the same pool
steps: Unit 1: start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of one connection.
Checkpoint `unit1-after-write`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(). Then arm the client-side fault: the next top-level ROLLBACK fails in the driver and is not sent.
Raise an application error inside the transaction. The framework attempts ROLLBACK, which fails, so the connection keeps its open transaction.
When the fault fires, before the framework sees its error, the adapter's driver layer reports checkpoint `after-fault` (the backend PID): the runner records the fault's effect on the server.
Checkpoint `after-unit1`: report the same backend PID; the runner records that session's state.

Unit 2, the next unit of work on the same pool: start a transaction, write the marker `next`, checkpoint `unit2-after-write` (report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid()), and end normally. Give up after settings.bound_ms and report the unit as pending.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: Unrelated work never runs inside, or commits, a transaction whose rollback failed: that transaction is never committed, and the next unit of work runs in a transaction of its own.
After the failure, the next unit of work on the same pool completes within the bound (settings.bound_ms) and commits.

execution.description: Negative control. Connection.commit() returning is reported as committed, including when the driver state was FAILED. A thrown commit() is reported as rolled_back. A failed Connection.rollback(Savepoint) is ignored and the outer transaction is committed. A thrown Connection.rollback() is followed by Connection.setAutoCommit(true), and the connection is kept. Connection.setTransactionIsolation is not called. A write made before a savepoint is executed inside that savepoint. One DriverManager connection is held. It is not a pool.
execution.form: One DriverManager connection is held and handed to the next unit. This is not a connection pool. correct closes it when Connection.rollback() throws. unsafe calls Connection.setAutoCommit(true) and keeps it.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A client-side injection in the adapter's driver layer (node-postgres, pg.Client.prototype.query): the top-level ROLLBACK fails without being sent, as a failed send would.
fault.preconditions: The framework's statements pass through the instrumented pg module (recorded as trace_sees_framework_pg).
fault.expected_server: Unit 1's transaction stays open on its connection ("idle in transaction"), holding the doomed write.
fault.expected_client: An error from the framework's rollback; what the framework then does with the connection is under test.

knowledge: The framework knows that its ROLLBACK failed, so it knows that the connection's transaction state is unknown.

api_outcome.basis: the body threw and Connection.rollback() threw. Connection.setAutoCommit(true) returned and the connection was kept.
api_outcome.contract: The unsafe jdbc-control policy reports committed whenever Connection.commit() returns, whatever PgConnection.getTransactionState() was before the call. It reports rolled_back when Connection.commit() throws. It calls Connection.commit() after Connection.rollback(Savepoint) has thrown. When Connection.rollback() throws, it calls Connection.setAutoCommit(true) and keeps the connection. Java 21 Connection.setAutoCommit says: "If this method is called during a transaction and the auto-commit mode is changed, the transaction is committed." pgjdbc 42.7.14 PgConnection.setAutoCommit(true) calls commit() when auto-commit is off. It does not call Connection.setTransactionIsolation. A write made before a nested savepoint is executed inside that savepoint.

error.message: injected client-side failure: ROLLBACK was not sent

unit2.basis: Connection.commit() returned. The driver state before the call was OPEN.

preconditions.description: the write of marker "doomed" had reached PostgreSQL at `unit1-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the write of marker "next" had reached PostgreSQL at `unit2-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the client-side fault (client-reject) fired exactly once
the next unit of work was attempted
the withheld ROLLBACK left unit 1's transaction open: its session was in a transaction holding unit 1's ID
preconditions.detail: at `after-fault`: session "idle in transaction", backend_xid 4039; transactionid locks [4039]
